title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet so Dots AI agents can make purchases
variety_exception: Assigned subject was tech; an AI-and-apps launch is a higher-priority tier and the day's strongest fresh tech story.

Amazon blocking Meta's Muse agents). Headline coverage also seen at CNBC, Reuters, Mashable.

slides.headline: ChatGPT can now spend your money.

image.credit: Illustrative photo: online card purchase / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0

slides.text:
OpenAI is rolling out ChatGPT Wallet, starting November 13.
Your Dots AI agents can use a card you add to buy things you ask for.

But not without you.
Every single purchase needs your sign-off, plus a Face ID or fingerprint check.

image.credit: Illustrative photo: contactless payment / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 4.0

slides.text:
Like Apple Pay, the agent never sees your real card number.
It gets a payment token instead.
For now it is U.S. only, for ChatGPT Pro members 18 and older.

OpenAI expects people to eventually let agents buy on their own.
You would set spending limits, categories or time periods first.

image.credit: Illustrative photo: online shopping / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0

slides.text:
The catch: some stores block AI agents.
Earlier this year Amazon blocked Meta's Muse agents.
Would you let a bot check out for you?

caption:
OpenAI just gave its AI agents a way to pay.

ChatGPT Wallet is rolling out starting November 13 for ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the U.S. who are 18 or older and have a U.S. billing address. It works with eligible American Express, Chase, Mastercard and Visa cards.

Once you add a card, OpenAI's Dots agents can buy things in response to your prompts. They check in before every checkout, and each purchase needs a security check with Face ID or a fingerprint.

Like tap to pay, the wallet swaps your real card details for a payment token, so neither the agent nor the store sees the actual number.

OpenAI says it eventually expects people to hand purchases to an agent entirely, within limits they set, such as a spending cap, a category or a time period.

There is a snag. Some retailers restrict AI agents or block them. Earlier this year Amazon blocked Meta's Muse agents. OpenAI says sites must make sure agents are not blocked by accident, and payment systems must recognize legitimate agent purchases.

Source: The Verge, OpenAI
